title: Looking inside: a projection of the learned states, and a grid of layers that saturate or do not
summary: Two SciML diagnostics of a learned model's inner workings. A principal-component plot shows the states it visits as a thin, almost one-dimensional sheet; a grid of small panels shows, for each architecture variant, how much of the first layer is saturated and how large the activation slope is.

media.alt: A fifteen-panel grid, three columns by five rows, each a small chart with a title like version 1.3. In most panels a solid red horizontal line sits at one on the left axis and a noisy dashed cyan curve near the bottom on a logarithmic right axis. In three panels with green titles the solid line is at zero and the dashed curve stays near one at the top.

source.caption: First-layer saturation across a 16-version normalization ablation
source.note: DISCLOSURE: the saturation grid's panel titles are internal version labels of an unpublished normalization ablation; they are not named here. Only the generic reading of saturation and the latent projection is taught.
group: 12_saturation_curve_grid_L1: First-layer saturation across a 16-version normalization ablation

read_the_figure.question: Is the learned representation using the capacity it has, and is any layer stuck at its limits?
read_the_figure.axes: Saturation grid: training step (0 to 2000) on the horizontal axis; left axis 0 to 1 is the fraction of first-layer pre-activations with magnitude above 3 (solid); right axis, logarithmic, is the mean slope of tanh (dashed cyan). Latent plot: first and second principal components of the integrated states, colour is the initial temperature.
look_at: Solid line at 1.0 (red titles): every first-layer unit sits in the flat part of tanh for all inputs. Solid line at 0 (green titles): none do.
Dashed cyan curve: where the solid line is 1 the mean slope is tiny and noisy, which is the vanishing gradient in a number; where the solid line is 0 the slope stays near 1.
The colour of the titles divides the panels into two groups; the legend at the bottom explains it. Only a minority of variants avoid saturation.

Latent plot: the axis labels show the share of variance of each component, about 100 percent for the first and about 0 percent for the second. All trajectories lie along one line, coloured by initial temperature.
In that plot a handful of short curved strokes sit apart on the left: a separate group of trajectories at the cold end of the temperature range.
read_the_figure.proves: A saturated first layer cannot pass gradient information back, however long training runs. A latent space that is a line means the model has discovered a one-parameter family; whether it is physically meaningful depends on whether the coordinate along it is the quantity you expect.
if_wrong: Fraction of saturated units at 1.0 from step 0: the inputs are too large for the first-layer weights; rescale inputs or initialization.
A mean slope of 1e-8: gradients to that layer are numerically zero.
A latent plot with variance share 100 and 0 percent: one component explains everything, so a second axis carries no information; it may also reflect different units, not structure.
Colouring by one variable only: a different colouring (time, species) may reveal other structure.
must_check: That the saturation threshold (here 3) is stated and the slope is on a log axis.
That the projection method and variance shares are printed.
That every panel in a grid has the same axes so the comparison is fair.
That the meaning of any colour coding is in the figure, not only in the caption.

terms.meaning: A unit whose input is so large in magnitude that its output is on the flat part of the activation.
The derivative 1 - tanh^2 z; tends to 0 for large |z|.
Orthogonal directions ordered by the variance of the data along them.
The fraction of total variance explained by a component.
The low-dimensional set that the hidden states actually occupy.
Small multiples of the same diagnostic across variants of a design.

remember: For tanh, |z| > 3 means the slope is below 0.01.
A saturated layer passes almost no gradient.
The principal components of centred data are the eigenvectors of its covariance.
A variance share of 100 percent for one component means the data lie on a line in that representation.
Small multiples need shared axes and a legend that explains every colour.

steps.title: Why |z| above 3 is called saturated
steps.note: At the threshold used in the figure the slope is already one percent. Beyond it, the slope falls exponentially: tanh'(z) is about 4 exp(-2|z|).

steps.title: Gradient through one saturated layer
steps.note: The activation slope multiplies the backward signal element by element. With slopes near 1e-8 as in the red panels, the update to the first layer is numerically nothing.

steps.title: Principal components
steps.tex: C=\frac1N\sum_i(x_i-\bar x)(x_i-\bar x)^{\mathsf T}=V\Lambda V^{\mathsf T},\qquad \text{share}_k=\frac{\lambda_k}{\sum_j\lambda_j}
steps.note: The two axes of the latent plot are the first two columns of V. A first share near 100 percent says the states are nearly collinear after centring.

steps.title: A line is a one-parameter family
steps.note: If the colour varies monotonically along the line, the single coordinate encodes the initial temperature; the strokes are the time evolution at each T0.

worked.title: Slope at the threshold
worked.problem: Compute tanh'(3) and compare it with 4 exp(-6).
worked.answer: About 0.0099 either way: below 1 percent of the slope at the origin.

analyze.q: A panel has a solid line at 1.0 for the whole run. Name two causes at the level of data scaling or initialization.
Why is the dashed slope curve noisier in the red panels than in the green ones?
analyze.hint: Tiny numbers on a log axis.

analyze.q: The first principal component carries nearly all the variance. Does that mean the system has one degree of freedom?
analyze.hint: Units and scaling of the inputs.

evaluate.q: Would you keep a variant that never saturates but has a worse loss? Which other figures would you want?
What additional colouring would you try for the latent plot to test if the line is just temperature?

create: Make a single summary panel: saturation fraction at the end of training for all variants, sorted, with the three non-saturating ones marked.
Re-draw the latent plot after standardizing each variable and compare the variance shares.

checks.q: What does the solid line measure?
checks.answer: The fraction of first-layer pre-activations with magnitude above 3.

checks.q: Why does saturation of the first layer stop learning there even though later layers still train?
checks.answer: The gradient to the first layer is multiplied by the slope of its own activation, about 1e-8 here, so its parameters hardly move.

checks.q: A latent plot shows 100 percent of variance on one axis. Is the model's representation good?
checks.answer: Not necessarily: the dominant axis may reflect one variable of large magnitude. Standardize before reading shares.

checks.q: Propose a figure of one number per variant that summarizes the whole saturation grid.
checks.answer: Dot plot of end-of-training saturated fraction with the mean slope as marker size, sorted.
